what-a-skill-is-made-of.header: What a skill is made of
what-a-skill-is-made-of.description: A skill is a folder with a required SKILL.md (a name and a description, then the instructions) and optional scripts/, references/ and assets/ folders [1]. ChatGPT describes the same three parts in its own words: a name and description, workflow steps and supporting materials [2].

names-differ-by-app.description: Claude, ChatGPT and Codex say “Skills”, GitHub Copilot says “agent skills”, and the Gemini app turns Gems into skills for personal accounts on 17 December 2026 [1]. Whether the Gemini app's skills are SKILL.md folders is not stated in the pages read; it is verified for Gemini CLI only [2].

the-description-is-the-routing-line.header: The description is the routing line
the-description-is-the-routing-line.description: Google's Day 3 whitepaper calls the description “your routing algorithm” [1]. This is Google's framing of how a skill is chosen, not a measurement of how often it routes correctly.

anthropics-definition-of-a-skill.description: Anthropic defines skills as “folders that include instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude can load when needed” [1]. The Slide quotes the sentence as written; “Claude” in it is Anthropic's product, and the Agent Skills standard (note 1) publishes the same folder format for other agents.

name-and-use-when.title: Name and use-when
name-and-use-when.script: A skill is a folder of instructions, and the company that introduced skills says so in almost those words. The folder holds one file it cannot do without, and that file starts with a name and a description, one line saying when to use it. That line matters more than it looks, because it is the first thing the model sees and, as you'll hear in a minute, often the only thing. On our card it is the title and the “use when” line in the head.

steps-in-the-body.title: Steps in the body
steps-in-the-body.script: Then come the instructions, the procedure itself as numbered steps, in the body of the card. Beside that file a skill can carry optional supporting files that its steps reach for, like a species guide, a label template or an arm preset tucked into the card's sleeve. So a skill is a procedure, plus the material that procedure needs.

for-developers.title: For developers
for-developers.script: If you work with a coding agent, switch to the coding-agent view, where the two parts of the file are called its frontmatter and the body of SKILL.md, and you can open and edit each. If you don't, you can ignore that view completely.
